description: How money moves electronically: payment systems, clearing and settlement, cards and online payments, the architecture of mobile money platforms, agent networks, USSD and app channels, interoperability between providers, and fraud and consumer protection, with Ghana's GhIPSS and mobile money market as the running case. Students design and simulate a working mobile money system in the browser, posting every transaction to a double-entry ledger and tracing it through the switch, the agent and the USSD menu.
modelledOn: CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures
ISO 20022 and ISO 8583 financial messaging standards
PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)
GSMA Mobile Money API specification and Mobile Money Certification
outcomes: Explain how payment systems clear and settle transactions and compare gross and net settlement and their risks.
Describe the card and online payment flows, their message standards and the security controls that protect them.
Design the architecture of a mobile money platform, including wallets, a double-entry ledger, the trust account and its APIs.
Analyse agent network operations, including float, liquidity and commissions, and USSD and app channel design.
Explain how interoperability between providers is achieved through a national switch and how disputes and reversals are handled.
Identify common payment fraud and evaluate controls, KYC tiers and consumer protection rules set by regulators.

units.title: Money, payments and payment systems
topics: Functions of money; cash, central bank money, commercial bank money and e-money
Payment instruments: cash, cheques, credit transfers, direct debits, cards, mobile money and QR payments
Parties in a payment: payer, payee, their providers, the switch or scheme, the settlement agent and the regulator
The payments landscape in Ghana and Africa: the Bank of Ghana, GhIPSS, banks, electronic money issuers and fintechs
Financial inclusion: why mobile money spread in Africa, from M-Pesa in Kenya to Ghana's mobile money market

units.title: Payment systems and clearing
topics: Clearing and settlement: authorisation, clearing, netting and settlement; finality and irrevocability
Real-time gross settlement (the Ghana Interbank Settlement system) versus deferred net settlement (ACH)
Cheque codeline clearing, ACH direct credits and debits, and instant payment systems such as GhIPSS Instant Pay
Settlement risk, liquidity risk and credit risk; collateral, prefunding and intraday liquidity
Payment messages: ISO 20022 structure (pacs, pain and camt messages) and migration from legacy formats
Simulating netting across banks and computing settlement positions

units.title: Cards and online payments
topics: Card schemes and the four-party model: issuer, acquirer, scheme, merchant and cardholder; interchange and the merchant discount rate
Card transaction flow: authorisation, clearing and settlement; ISO 8583 messages and response codes
Chip cards and EMV: cryptograms, offline and online authentication; contactless payment
Online payments: payment gateways, 3-D Secure, tokenisation, chargebacks and card-not-present fraud
PCI DSS requirements and reducing scope with hosted payment pages and tokens
National card schemes such as gh-link and regional switching

units.title: Mobile money architecture
topics: The mobile money model: electronic money issuer, trust account at a bank, e-value backed one-to-one by funds
Platform architecture: wallet service, double-entry ledger, transaction engine, fees and limits, notification service
Transaction types: cash-in, cash-out, person-to-person transfer, merchant payment, bill payment, bulk disbursement
Correctness under failure: atomic transactions, idempotency keys, reconciliation and handling timeouts
APIs for merchants and partners; the GSMA Mobile Money API and callback design
Regulation: the Payment Systems and Services Act 2019 (Act 987), licence categories and trust account rules

units.title: Agent networks
topics: The role of agents: cash-in and cash-out points that turn e-value into cash and back
Agent hierarchy: master agents, sub-agents and merchants; recruitment, training and supervision
Liquidity management: e-float and cash float, rebalancing, and running out of float on market days
Commission structures, agent economics and the viability of rural agents
Agent fraud and errors: split transactions, unauthorised withdrawals, and agent monitoring
Simulating an agent network and the float rebalancing across a district

units.title: USSD and app channels
topics: USSD as a channel: sessions, shortcodes, menu trees, session timeouts and USSD gateway integration
Designing USSD menus for low literacy and feature phones: menu depth, confirmations, PIN entry and local languages
Smartphone apps, SIM toolkit applications and their security trade-offs
QR code payments and interoperable QR (GhQR); NFC and the move to merchant acceptance
Building and usability-testing a USSD mobile money menu in the browser simulator

units.title: Interoperability between providers
topics: Closed-loop versus interoperable systems; bilateral links versus a central switch
The GhIPSS Mobile Money Interoperability platform: wallet-to-wallet and wallet-to-bank transfers
Switch design: routing, name enquiry, transaction status queries, reversals and dispute resolution
Settlement between providers: net positions, settlement windows and reconciliation files
Cross-border payments and remittances: corridors, correspondent banking and the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS)
Interoperability elsewhere in Africa: Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda and the WAEMU zone compared

units.title: Fraud and consumer protection
topics: Common mobile money fraud: social engineering, fake reversal requests, SIM swap, PIN theft and insider fraud
Fraud detection: velocity rules, device and location signals, anomaly detection and case management
Customer due diligence and KYC tiers with the Ghana Card; transaction and balance limits
Consumer protection: transparent fees, complaint handling, dispute timelines and dormant accounts
Taxes and levies on electronic transfers and their effect on usage

units.title: The future of payments and capstone
topics: Central bank digital currencies: the eCedi pilot, design choices and offline payments
Open banking and payment APIs; super-apps and embedded finance
Savings and credit on mobile money: digital susu, nano-loans and their risks
Capstone: design and simulate an interoperable mobile money service with a USSD menu, a ledger, agents and settlement through a switch
